intro: More parts of the body, what they do, and how people are at different moments.
p.pulmón.consejo: In the plural it loses the accent: «pulmones». We have two, one on each side of the chest.
p.hombro.consejo: The h is silent: «OM-bro». «Con la mochila al hombro» means carrying the bag slung over it.
p.cintura.consejo: It belongs to the family of «cinturón» (belt), which is fastened right at the waist.
p.muñeca.consejo: The ñ sounds «ny»: mu-NYE-ka. It is also a toy shaped like a person (a doll).
p.codo.consejo: «Hablar por los codos» means to talk a lot, non-stop.
p.postura.consejo: It looks like English «posture». A good posture takes care of your back.
p.respirar.consejo: The initial r sounds strong: rres-pi-RAR. «Respira hondo» means to take in a lot of air.
p.soltar.consejo: The o becomes ue: «suelto», «sueltas». It is the opposite of «agarrar» (to grab).
p.oler.consejo: The o becomes «hue»: «huelo», «huele». To say what something smells of, use «oler a».
p.embarazada.consejo: False friend: it means «pregnant», not «embarrassed». For embarrassed, say «avergonzada».
p.anciano.consejo: It is respectful. The woman is «anciana». «Persona mayor» is another kind way to say it.
p.distraído.consejo: It comes from «distraer». With «estar» it is a moment; with «ser», a trait.
p.lástima.consejo: «¡Qué lástima!» is what you say when something is a pity. Also: «me da lástima».
p.actitud.consejo: It looks like «attitude», but with «ct» and no final e. «Tener buena actitud» is very common.
b1.titulo: The body and how we are
b1.texto:
Today we see more parts of the body and new ways of talking about it.

- **From the neck down:** the **hombro** (shoulder), the **pecho** (chest), the **cintura** (waist). On the arm, the **codo** (elbow) and the **muñeca** (wrist). Inside, the **pulmones** (lungs).
- **What the body does:** **respirar** (to breathe), **saltar** (to jump), **soltar** (to let go of) something you were holding, **oler** (to smell) a flower.
- **Ages:** a **recién nacido** (newborn), a child, an adult, an **anciano** (elderly man).
- **How we are:** with **estar** and an adjective, for example **está embarazada** or **está distraído**.
- **Attitude:** **tener** a positive attitude. And when something is a shame: **¡Qué lástima!**
b2.f0.texto: Sit down properly and relax your shoulders.
b2.f1.texto: My elbow and my wrist hurt.
b2.f2.texto: Your posture in front of the computer is to blame.
b2.f3.texto: My chest hurts when I jump or run.
b2.f5.texto: Now breathe in deeply and let the air out little by little.
b2.f6.texto: I can already feel that I am breathing better.
b2.f7.texto: It is a pity not to have come sooner.
b4.texto:
Some verbs change the **o** of the stem into **ue** when that syllable carries the stress:

- **soltar** → suelto, sueltas, suelta, soltamos, soltáis, sueltan
- **oler** → **huelo**, hueles, huele, olemos, oléis, huelen
- **poder**, **volver**, **dormir** and **doler** change in the same way.

In **nosotros** and **vosotros** the stress falls on the ending, and the **o** does not change: **soltamos**, **olemos**.

At the start of a word, the sound «ue» is written **hue-**: that is why it is **huele**. To say what something smells of, use **oler a**: huele a café.
b4.e0.texto: Let go of the rope slowly.
b4.e1.texto: The kitchen smells of warm bread.
b4.e2.texto: The children smell the flowers in the garden.
b5.f0.texto: The park smells of wet grass and fresh earth.
b5.f1.texto: An elderly man with a straight back walks slowly among the trees.
b5.f2.texto: He carries his shoulders relaxed and his hands behind his back.
b5.f3.texto: Every ten steps he stops, closes his eyes and breathes deeply.
b5.f4.texto: The cold air fills his lungs and clears his head.
b5.f5.texto: A distracted young man arrives running, with his backpack on his shoulder.
b5.f6.texto: He sits on the bench and sighs with his chest heaving.
b5.f7.texto: The old man smiles and shows him a simple posture.
b5.f8.texto: He raises his arms, drops the backpack and closes his eyes.
b5.f9.texto: Little by little, his attitude becomes calmer.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! The lungs fill with air when you breathe.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The waist is the narrow part of the body; it is not used to breathe.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The wrist joins hand and arm. We breathe with the lungs.
b6.pregunta: Which part of the body do we breathe with?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Hueles» is for «tú». The subject is «la cocina».
b7.o1.refuerzo: That's it! The o becomes «hue»: la cocina huele.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive is not conjugated. Here you need «huele».
b8.frase: Suelte el aire poco a poco
b8.traduccion: Let the air out little by little
b9.o0.refuerzo: That would be «está avergonzada». It is a false friend of «embarrassed».
b9.o1.refuerzo: For that you say «está ocupada». Here there is a baby on the way.
b9.pregunta: Mi hermana está embarazada. What does it mean?
b11.o1.refuerzo: Posture is how you place your body, not a feeling.
b11.o2.refuerzo: The waist is a body part. Here you need a word of sorrow.
b11.pregunta: You are sorry that you cannot come. What is missing?
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Anciano» is about age, not about attention.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That's it! A distracted person loses focus easily.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Embarazada» describes a state of health, not attention.
b12.pregunta: Which word describes someone who does not pay attention?
p.siéntese.consejo: From «sentarse»; the formal command ends in «-e», as in «siéntese».
p.relaje.consejo: From «relajar»; the j sounds like a Spanish h: «relaje».
p.culpa.consejo: Think of «culpable»: the one who has the «culpa» is the one to blame.
p.ordenador.consejo: In Spain «ordenador» is the usual word for computer; Latin America often says «computadora».
p.salto.consejo: The noun and the verb form look the same; the context shows which one it is.
p.corro.consejo: From «correr»; the rr sounds strong, as in «corro».
p.músculos.consejo: The stress falls on the first syllable: «MUS-cu-los», as the accent suggests.
p.suelta.consejo: From «soltar»: «suelta» is the he or she form.
p.cuerda.consejo: «Cuerda» can also mean a string or a clock spring; the context shows which.
p.huelen.consejo: From «oler»; the o becomes «ue», as in «huelen».
p.relajados.consejo: From «relajar»: «relajado» describes someone calm and without tension.
p.pulmones.consejo: «Pulmones» is usually plural, like the two lungs.
p.despeja.consejo: From «despejar», which also means to clear your mind.
p.corriendo.consejo: The gerund of «correr» is «corriendo»: the e becomes i.
p.agitado.consejo: «Agitado» describes fast breathing or a restless person.
